seesaw_periods.comparison: Kudla's seesaw identity interchanges theta lifts in a convergent pairing. Lean assumes weighted finite evaluation functionals, two families of edges and a spanning condition on test vectors for which two kernels agree and the lifted periods are proportional. It transfers that proportionality to the descended periods, with one scalar for every index. The proof extends a finite-sum identity by linearity and spanning. Give the classical identity and this additional inference distinct entries when writing the note.
sources: Kudla, Seesaw dual reductive pairs, §1, adjointness (1.9) and seesaw identity (1.14)

sphericalCompat_std.verdict: Standard definite-unitary specialization of automorphic attachment, with polynomial annihilation at spherical places
sphericalCompat_std.comparison: Over an embedded CM field E with CM type and Weil data (including a primitive 5040th root and a splitting character), take any nonempty finite rank and any finite w. Every eigenform of the standard definite group has an attached representation. Attached means continuous, trace-nondegenerate, with coefficientwise ℓ-adic approximation to the prescribed Hecke polynomials in the project's mostFrobenii filter. Every attached r satisfies, when the full local maximal compact fixes f, unramifiedness away from ℓ or crystallinity above ℓ, and the prescribed jumps above ℓ. The additional Hecke-polynomial clause is conditional on HasHeckePolyAt at a split w. It requires annihilation on a geometric Frobenius away from ℓ, and on period Frobenius above ℓ. Chenevier–Harris Theorem 3.2.3 starts with regular polarized cuspidal GL data and identifies the characteristic polynomial at spherical w|ℓ. BLGGT Theorem 2.1.1 supplies full away-from-ℓ parameter compatibility and crystalline/jump assertions. Labesse Corollaire 5.3 supplies weak base change, generally an isobaric sum. Transport between unitary eigenforms, GL constituents and the specified weights is necessary. Within that correspondence the polynomial annihilator and the filter notion of attachment retain less than characteristic-polynomial equality and full local compatibility.
sources: G. Chenevier and M. Harris, Construction of automorphic Galois representations, II, Camb. J. Math. 1 (2013), General Hypotheses 1.1, p. 57, Theorem 3.2.3(a′)–(d), pp. 66–67. At a spherical place above ℓ the theorem identifies the characteristic polynomial of crystalline Frobenius.
T. Barnet-Lamb, T. Gee, D. Geraghty and R. Taylor, Potential automorphy and change of weight, Ann. of Math. 179 (2014), Theorem 2.1.1, p. 538, especially clauses (2)–(4).
J.-P. Labesse, Changement de base CM et séries discrètes, Corollaire 5.3, pp. 43–44 of the author's text. Weak base change gives an isobaric sum and local matching at unramified and split places.
Pinned definitions of Attached and SphericalCompat.
Pinned definitions of good type, finite type, jumps and PolyKillsAt in the two residue-characteristic cases.

staircase_harmonic_highest.verdict: The forward highest-vector construction by products of minors, in ordered and determinant-twisted coordinates.
staircase_harmonic_highest.comparison: Kashiwara–Vergne III, Proposition 6.1 and its proof exhibit products of initial minors in one block and terminal minors in the other as pluriharmonic highest vectors when their row lengths fit. Theorem 6.3 gives their compact weights. Davidson Theorem 2.9 prints the products, the partition differences giving their powers, and the compact weights. Lean orders arbitrary finite index sets by the supplied injective parameters and uses the positive and negative blocks in those orders. Its restrictions on the two sets of occupied heights ensure disjoint rows and enough columns of each sign. The returned weights include the vacuum and determinant-character shifts explicitly, with the compact-side weight supplied by hw. Only the displayed polynomials and the forward assertion are used. The declaration ranges over heights strictly below the compact dimension.
sources: Kashiwara and Vergne, On the Segal–Shale–Weil representations and harmonic polynomials, Chapter III, Proposition 6.1, formula (6.2) and Theorem 6.3, p. 44
Davidson, The harmonic representation of U(p,q), §2, Theorem 2.9, p. 45

witt.verdict: Witt extension in matrix coordinates for a nondegenerate Hermitian form with a nontrivial field involution.
witt.comparison: A left inverse for each column map makes its columns a basis of its image. Equality of the two restricted Gram matrices gives an isometry between these subspaces, even when their restriction is degenerate. Every subspace of this finite-dimensional field vector space is a summand. The ambient Hermitian form is invertible. The assumed z with z−z* nonzero gives a trace-one element for the conversion to the quadratic-space statement. First's Corollary 4.9 extends the isometry to the ambient unitary group, giving exactly gX=Y. For this field and involution the converse coordinate formulation of extension follows by choosing columns for the subspace.
sources: First, Witt's extension theorem for quadratic spaces over semiperfect rings, Remark 2.1 and Corollary 4.9, p. 16 of preprint

witt_Ohat_of_orthonormal.verdict: Integral extension of two orthonormal frames, applied separately on the finite-place orbits of conjugation.
witt_Ohat_of_orthonormal.comparison: An orthonormal frame over the integral finite adèles splits off a free summand, with projection given by its adjoint. Matching the columns of two frames gives an isometry of summands. Apply First's extension result on each conjugation orbit of local integer rings, then assemble their integral isometries and inverses to obtain an element of Kf. Each local ring, or the product for one split pair, is semiperfect. The whole infinite product need not be. The integral element z with z−z* a unit gives a trace-one element z/(z−z*) for interpreting the Hermitian forms in First's quadratic-space convention.
sources: First, Witt's extension theorem for quadratic spaces over semiperfect rings, Remark 2.1 and Corollary 4.9. Corollary 4.11 concerns generation by quasi-reflections
